findingDetails.title: v2 bridge drops sk-vision's chat.message hook although research records a v2 destination for it
findingDetails.claim: MAPPED_HOOKS omits chat.message, so sk-vision's chat.message handler never runs on OpenCode 2; the only signal is cleanup.skippedKeys, which no dispatcher inspects.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Searched the bridge tests and the plugins README for an explicit acceptance of the skip. v2-bridge.test.cjs:632 asserts skippedKeys === ['chat.message'] for a stub plugin, and README:175 states an unmapped key is reported through cleanup.skippedKeys -- so the skipping mechanism is intended and tested.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The omission may be a deliberate scope cut because ctx.session.hook('prompt') semantics were unverified at port time, with the skip treated as the safe default rather than a parity requirement.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Upgrades to P1 if any phase child's acceptance criteria or the feature-catalog entry for sk-vision claims v2 parity for its pre-submit path; downgrades to informational if a phase doc records chat.message as an accepted v2 gap.

findingDetails.title: Dispatch version resolver returns 'unknown' for a path-qualified binary, silently downgrading a v1 error rule to a warning
findingDetails.claim: resolveOpencodeVersionSync bails to 'unknown' whenever the binary contains a path separator, while the rule engine deliberately matches path-qualified binaries. With version 'unknown', dispatch-rule-checks.mjs:319 downgrades every non-both-version rule to warn, so command-flag-for-slash-prompt stops blocking a v1 run whose slash prompt lacks --command.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Looked for a caller that supplies options.version explicitly, which would bypass the sync resolver, and for a documented rationale for the separator bail. The evaluate() signature accepts options.version but no caller in the reviewed files passes it. The bail mirrors hasPathSeparator at :143, which predates the dual-version work, and the runtime resolver at opencode-version.cjs:188 accepts a path-qualified OPENCODE_BIN -- so the two resolvers disagree on the same input.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Fail-open is the file's declared doctrine (a guard that cannot resolve its binary must not invent a refusal); the separator bail may be that doctrine applied uniformly, accepting a lost refusal on the path-qualified shape.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Upgrades to P1 if a supported install shape (the documented opencode2 launcher called by absolute path) is verified to reach this branch with a slash prompt; downgrades to informational if the PreToolUse caller always passes options.version.

findingDetails.title: Async probe timeout cannot bound the default probe, which runs synchronously on the event loop
findingDetails.claim: probeWithTimeout races a 3000ms timer against Promise.resolve().then(() => probe(binary)). The default probe is probeBinary, a synchronous spawnSync, so the timer cannot fire until the probe has already returned; the only real bound is spawnSync's own timeout. The function therefore advertises a hard deadline it does not enforce for the path that ships.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether an injected async deps.probe makes the race meaningful (it does) and whether spawnSync kills its child on timeout (it does, and returns an error that maps to 'unknown'). Runtime impact is therefore bounded at the same 3000ms by a different mechanism.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The race is a seam for injected probes in tests and for a future async probe, not a claim about the default path.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrades to informational if the docstring is amended to state that the default probe is bounded by spawnSync and the race only governs injected probes.

searchLedger.invariant: Every hook key a shipped plugin returns must either be mapped by the bridge or be recorded as an accepted v2 gap.

searchActions.result: in-scope plugins return event, tool, dispose, tool.execute.before/after and experimental.chat.system.transform; sk-vision additionally returns chat.message and config
chat.message is recorded as having a v2 destination (ctx.session.hook('prompt'))

searchLedger.rationale: An unmapped key with a recorded v2 destination means a shipped plugin loses a hook on v2 with no operator-visible signal.

searchLedger.hypothesis: A path-qualified opencode2 invocation resolves to 'unknown' and loses the v1-only blocking rules.

searchActions.result: sync resolver bails at :186; evaluate() downgrades non-both appliesTo rules to warn at :319
command-flag-for-slash-prompt is severity error with appliesTo [v1]; v2-slash-prompt-route is warn with appliesTo [v2]

searchLedger.rationale: The rule engine matches path-qualified binaries by design while the resolver refuses to probe them, so the refusal is lost on a real install shape.

searchLedger.hypothesis: The async probe deadline is not enforced for the shipped synchronous probe.

searchActions.result: spawnSync runs inside a microtask, so the racing timer cannot fire first

searchLedger.rationale: A deadline that cannot fire on the default path is a false affordance; impact is bounded by spawnSync's own timeout, hence P2.

searchLedger.hypothesis: The v2 builder drops --dir and the child inherits the parent cwd.

searchActions.result: builder sets cwd (:2431); dispatch destructures commandCwd (:3509); spawn passes cwd (:3767)

searchLedger.ruledOutReason: cwd is threaded from the builder to the spawn, so the v2 child runs in options.directoryRoot exactly as the v1 child does via --dir.

searchLedger.hypothesis: The v2 model selector accepts a #variant suffix as the builder emits it.

searchActions.result: v2 emits -m <model>#<effort>; the v2 CLI contract for the # suffix was not verified this iteration

searchLedger.deferredReason: Needs the cli-opencode SKILL.md invocation contract and the research record's variant verdict; that document is not yet read, so the shape is neither confirmed nor refuted.

searchLedger.hypothesis: The v2 tool transform can throw on a plugin whose tool args are a ZodObject rather than a raw shape, or on a zod version without toJSONSchema.

searchActions.result: tool definitions declare a raw shape (args: { ... }), which z.object accepts

searchLedger.ruledOutReason: zod 4.1.8 provides z.toJSONSchema, and the reviewed tool definitions pass a raw shape.

searchLedger.hypothesis: sessionEventState leaks one entry per session for the life of the v2 process.

searchActions.result: each entry is a small Set deleted on session.deleted and on the two started events

searchLedger.ruledOutReason: No observed growth path: entries hold two strings and three event types clear them; recorded as an observation instead.

detail: Inventory map built over 159 manifest files across 16 subsystems; the four cross-cutting producers are lib/v2-bridge.js, the two version resolvers, dispatch-rule-checks.mjs and fanout-run.cjs.
16/16 plugin entry files default-export dualPlugin(id, server); zod is pinned 4.1.8 so the bridge's z.toJSONSchema call resolves.

cli-opencode dispatch splits by resolved version: v1 uses --dir/--variant/--dangerously-skip-permissions, v2 uses run --standalone/-m model#effort/--auto plus cwd. buildNativeLineageCommand refuses v2 with a stated reason.
hard-rules.json splits the slash-prompt family by appliesTo (v1 error / v2 warn), so the v1 rule no longer blocks valid v2 runs when the version resolves.

direction: v2 cli-opencode branch omits --dir, so the child runs in the wrong working directory
reason: The v2 builder sets cwd instead (:2431); the dispatch path destructures it as commandCwd (:3509) and the spawn passes cwd: commandCwd ?? process.cwd() (:3767). Equivalent to v1's --dir.

direction: one of the 16 plugins still exports a v1-only entry object

direction: sessionEventState grows without bound and leaks across sessions on v2
reason: Entries are keyed per session and deleted on session.execution.started, session.compaction.started and session.deleted; each value is a two-element Set, so no growth path was demonstrated in the reviewed code. Recorded as an observation, not a finding.
